description: Owner decision 2026-11-08. --backend takes short names meaning latest/default, with specific models selectable; definitions live in sc-agent-types. IDs confirmed from provider docs 2026-11-08: claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, claude-fable-5-1, gpt-6-luna, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra. No gpt-6-terra exists. Replaces anthropic_haiku and openai_luna; closes agt-ho2.
notes:
Scope per owner 2026-11-08: establish conventions for future agent work; only haiku and luna are tested as judge backends today. BACKENDS stays jev, haiku, luna (renamed; old names removed, closes agt-ho2). --backend takes the short name (latest) or a known model id of that backend. MODELS and ModelId gain sonnet, opus, fable, terra, sol, astra as definitions only with id round-trip tests, not selectable as judge backends and no wire testing. Build on top of PR 47 and the Jev layer; update REQ/ADR.
Owner 2026-11-08, added to scope. (1) ~/.sc-agent/models.toml with [[model]] rows id, alias, released, read at startup; a short name resolves to the newest released across crate and file; only existing short names; malformed file is CONFIG_INVALID; repo check.toml [models] still wins but is not the expected path. Add a read/list so the resolved model and its source (crate or file) can be seen. Available from the Rust and Python APIs too. (2) Local freshness test: asks Anthropic (Models API, line field) and OpenAI (models list) and fails when a provider lists a newer model in a tracked line than the crate MODELS table. Never runs in CI (CI env set); skips with a printed reason when no key or the network fails, so offline or keyless runs do not fail; fails only on a positive newer-model result. Update REQ/ADR.
Freshness test source, owner 2026-11-08: use the local CLIs, no API keys. Codex: codex debug models (JSON; slug, visibility; visibility list only). Claude: claude -p with --model <alias> --output-format stream-json --verbose, read model from the system init event, for haiku, sonnet, opus, fable. Both verified 2026-11-08 on CLI 0.166.0 and 2.1.316. Skip with a printed reason if a CLI is absent or its output does not parse; never run in CI. codex debug is not a stable interface, so parse failure must be visible in the skip reason.
Owner 2026-11-08: use codex debug models in the local freshness test, with code comments linking randlee/sc-agent#48. Agents maintain it, so a format change need not be hidden: if the CLI is present and its output no longer parses, the test fails with a clear message rather than skipping. Missing CLI still skips; never runs in CI. Supersedes the earlier skip-on-parse-failure note.
Owner-supplied live traces 2026-11-08: a funded key's valid request answered model jev-1.14.0, while the crate catalog says jev-1.13.0, so the catalog is behind. GET /v1/models exists on the Jev API and returned 200 with a funded key; the freshness test can use it for Jev. Whether it is billing-gated is untested.
QA c9a7b5c minors (not fixed): file-only model ids cannot be pinned with --backend; 'jev models' ignores check.toml [models]; check_date accepts 2026-02-31; an old-session error does not name the backend; codex non-zero exit is a hard failure in the freshness test; BackendRegistry::loopback_from_env ignores resolved models. models_file= gap closed by c855743. Freshness Jev source: GET /v1/models returns only jev-latest and jev-preview with release_date, so the test compares jev-latest release_date to the crate jev row.

title: Separate session and general loggers, both injectable with sc-agent defaults
description: Owner expectation (2026-11-08): sc-observability logging for both session and general logging, in separate logs, each injectable with a fallback default set by sc-agent. Today: only the session log exists, at <log_root>/logs/<service>.log.jsonl via sc_jev_host::ObservabilityAdapter. No general log: no crate but sc-jev-host links sc-observability and none uses tracing or log. Injection: sc_jev_check RunConfig::new(repo_root, SharedSessionLog) takes any SessionLog with no default; ComposeInputs (crates/sc-jev-host/src/compose.rs:125-224) has no logger setter and always opens the adapter (:374,:425); CLI and Python expose only a log_dir path. Needs: a general-log port, ComposeInputs setters for both with defaults, Python injection per the Python-parity rule, ADR-SAG-0013 amendment.
notes:
Owner 2026-11-08: logger injection is a Python wheel API concern, not a CLI one. CLI keeps sc-agent's default loggers and --log-dir. Python accepts injected session and general loggers, falling back to defaults.
Owner asked 2026-11-08 whether the sc-observability wheel's log can be injected. Yes in principle. sc_observability 1.5.0 Python wheel has Logger, create_logger, and a host path: Rust install_host_logger (bindings/python/sc-observability-py/src/lib.rs:919) with Python get_host_logger. sc_jev_py today links only the Rust crate via sc-jev-host, not the wheel. Options: (a) Python caller passes a sc_observability Logger; sc_jev_py adapts it to SessionLog by calling logger.log through Python (needs GIL, separate compiled modules can't share Rust types). (b) sc_jev_py installs its logger as host so Python attaches through get_host_logger. Wheel requires Python >=3.10, compatible with 3.11+. Not prototyped.
Owner 2026-11-08: GIL per row rejected; expects the same Rust logger working from the same binary. Direction: follow sc-observability ADR-015: sc_jev_py links the sc-observability-py rlib and its core backend, registers that module inside its own binary, and Rust writes rows directly with no GIL. Python gets the same logger from sc_jev_py (attached view). Python-through-logger and capsule options dropped; ADR-015 rejects capsule and cross-wheel Rust object transfer. ADR-015 describes an embedded interpreter; extension-module loading from python needs a prototype. Wheel's standalone sc_observability Logger stays a separate logger, so judge-jev should take its logger from sc_jev_py when both are used.
Owner correction 2026-11-08: the two logs are instantiate and use. The real gap is that general logging was not created before code was written: go through the code, add logging, and inject the logger everywhere it should have been from day one. Python: the fact sharing the logger is non-trivial is itself an issue, in sc-observability-py docs or implementation; find which and raise it there.
Checked 2026-11-08 against v1.5.0, by running a scratch cdylib on macOS arm64, Python 3.14: sharing works today from a separate extension, about 12 lines. Link sc-observability-py as _native, create_core_backend, wrap_pymodule!(_native), install_host_logger, seed sys.modules['sc_observability._native'], keep the Arc in a static, Rust try_log inside py.detach. 1000 rows no GIL; Python get_host_logger shares one queue and file. Blocker was a docs gap: ADR-015 reads as forbidding it. Pyo3 must be =0.29.2 in sc_jev_py. Not run: maturin path, Linux, Windows.

title: Streaming decision calls through one CLI instance
description: Owner expectation (2026-11-08): one sc-ai instance handles thousands of Jev or other decision queries by streaming, so callers don't spawn a process per query. Likely next phase. Today: sc-ai does one payload per run; backends run sequentially; JevClient thread-safety unverified. Design questions: JSONL over stdin and stdout, concurrency limit, shared rate limit across workers, ordering, partial failure and resume, cancellation, session-log writer, Python API, memory bounds. Plan-anchor runs at most 4 threads per batch.
notes:
Owner answers 2026-11-08. (a) One JSONL file, stdio stream, or Python call with many Jev requests runs in parallel at a tested degree, e.g. 8 HTTP requests. (b) Advanced: streaming over time into a queue, so early decisions can become follow-up queries in the same stream. Every answer must identify its question. Resume uses sc-sha256. Concurrency is a global setting with a hardcoded default set from testing, e.g. 8. Everything is exposed to Python, and Python may offer more flexibility than the CLI, never less. Design note: threads with a bounded queue likely cover (a) and (b) without tokio at this scale; test before deciding, including shared rate limit and a busy-retry budget.
Owner correction 2026-11-08: streaming is a small change, not a redesign: a bounded queue with N workers around the existing per-request Jev work, which stays the same. Resume and sha256 lookup are out of scope: lookup from an existing result is a general caching function, a separate concern that would apply to all calls if enabled. Concurrent log writing comes from sc-observability. Seams checked: JudgeBackend, Transport and SessionLog are Send + Sync; the adapter shares one logger by Arc. Remaining scope: JSONL in/out, answers identify their question, concurrency default from testing, Python call.

title: Plan: slate decider/laya/kev decision APIs (naming + boundary rule)
description:
Owner request 2026-11-07. This is a docs-only plan amendment with no new gates and nothing built in A.1.
1. Crate-naming convention in docs/architecture.md. sc-jev-* covers the Jev API, including Haiku and Luna through Jev schema I/O (sc-jev, sc-jev-backends, sc-jev-check, sc-jev-host). Each other decision API gets its own API-specific crates named after it: sc-decider*, sc-laya*, sc-kev*. sc-decision-* is the API-agnostic layer across all of them.
2. Roadmap: the first work after the MVP adds the decider crates, then the laya crates. Owner priority: decider is the first to try. kev comes later and is unscheduled.
3. ADR-SAG-0030 records the decision API families. sc-decision-schema is organized by versioned module per API: jev::v1 now, with decider:: and laya:: reserved for the post-MVP crates and kev:: reserved after that.
4. plan.md Owner decisions item, and the r-7 module-layout note: keep sc-decision-schema API-agnostic so the decider and laya crates plug in without changing the jev crates.
Sequence: after r-3b, before r-7.

Closure round: REQ-SAG-0726 row omits run_many summary and submit_line; plan note for agt-1aq; assert zero sends in validate-first test. Facade omits Batch, StreamRequest. in_flight doc; clone per retry slice; SubmitError lacks Display; Tally mutex rationale; RequestId accessors.

Possible later improvement (stress 2026-11-09): a closed output reader is noticed only at the next write. When nothing finishes for a long time (every worker in a long Retry-After wait), 'sc-ai jev stream | head -1' keeps running up to the busy-retry budget (90 s). Detecting a closed stdout without a write (poll/POLLHUP) would need a platform dependency; documented in ADR-SAG-0032 and --help for now.
Row-loss follow-ups (stress 2026-11-09): a 1 s stall dropped 320 rows in 1 of 25 Ctrl-C runs (the wait is now 10 s); the rows_dropped Warn row can itself drop; plain iteration at concurrency 64 can lose up to about 54 tail rows without finish() or with; non-QueueFull failures are counted as drops too, inflating the count.

value: Owner rule (2026-11-08): create and inject the general and session loggers before writing feature code, and log from day one. Logging is not added afterwards.

Owner decision (2026-11-08): Minor QA findings go to beads, from every reviewer, for the remaining phase A rounds. Blocking and Important must be fixed before merge. Tell the enforcer this explicitly in the handoff, since its gate text otherwise forbids deferral.
Owner decision (2026-11-07): the composition-root crate planned as sc-agent-compose is renamed sc-jev-host (the old name implied sc-compose templates / agent launch). Applied in r-3b.

Owner decision (2026-11-08): backend selection uses short names: jev, haiku, sonnet, opus, fable, luna, terra, sol, astra, each meaning that model's latest/default. Specific model versions can also be specified. These are sc-agent-types definitions. Long names anthropic_haiku and openai_luna go away; nothing has been released.

Owner decision (2026-11-08): streaming (agt-1aq) and general logging (agt-9eh) land before publishing phase A, after PR 47, PR 49 and short names (agt-akp). Order: short names, then loggers with logging added through the code, then the streaming queue.

Owner decision (2026-11-08): questions_sha256 identifies a question set, for comparing runs of the same questions against different state. payload_sha256 (renamed from prompt_sha256) is questions and state, backend-neutral, for the equal-input proof across backends. request_sha256 identifies an identical request per backend and model, for substituting a cached response. All exposed before sending. sc-agent builds no cache.

Owner decisions (2026-11-08) on Jev calls: (1) accept model jev or any supported version like jev-1.13.0; jev means latest and may break on API changes, which is expected and fixed by upgrading sc-agent. (2) Use f64 and never round in sc-agent; rounding is the consumer's job; combined stats return double precision. (3) Errors return as much or more detail than Jev returns, with a discriminated error id plus message on every path; out of tokens, busy and API error are distinct and handled differently. (4) Busy defaults to 5 attempts with 4 delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 seconds. (5) sc-agent computes the sc-sha256 of questions for cache lookup but does not create a cache.

Owner decision (2026-11-08): new models are added globally in ~/.sc-agent/models.toml without recompiling, not per repo. A short name resolves to the most recent model from the crate or that file. A local-only test fails when providers list a newer model than the crate table, forcing a crate upgrade.

Owner design (2026-11-08): sc-agent launches any LLM, not just decision models; Jev is about 10% of it. sc-agent-types knows Jev, Anthropic and Codex/OpenAI models. It holds no knowledge that Haiku or Luna act as Jev mocks; that stays behind the JevDecision trait. New repo is named sc-agent.

Owner design (2026-11-08): one request form only, the Jev API request. Jev, Haiku and Luna all implement a jev-decision trait and are passed the same data. Haiku and Luna adapt internally. No second canonical payload form.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): when the owner supplies real evidence, it settles the question. Don't send it back through reviewer rounds or ask them to confirm it. Stop process and ceremony that doesn't change the code.

Owner goal (2026-11-08): sc-agent with streaming and logging, so the owner can analyse 10k-20k samples and tune plan-anchor and judge-jev Python code in a separate session. Plan-anchor and judge-jev requirements are NOT inputs here; don't read those repos or add features for them.

Owner naming rule (2026-11-07, final): 'jev' = anything speaking the Jev API, including Haiku/Luna via Jev schema I/O (e.g. sc-jev-check, sc-jev-host). 'decision' = API-agnostic across decision APIs (decider, laya, jev, kev), e.g. sc-decision-schema. The composition-root crate (formerly sc-agent-compose) is sc-jev-host; sc-decision-host was an interim, superseded name.

Owner priority (2026-11-07): closing and merging sprints in order is the primary task; plan-hardening or other side work must not take focus from sprint closure. Keep side work in the background and keep driving dev->QA->merge.

Owner roadmap (2026-11-07): right after the MVP, add the decider crates first (the owner's first API to try), then laya. kev comes later. Each API gets its own sc-<api>* crates; sc-decision-* stays API-agnostic.

Owner rule (2026-11-07): any ceremony in plans that the owner did not specify or discuss is high priority for removal. Ceremony flags (ceremony-qa, ceremony-finding-screen) are inputs; the orchestrator uses judgement and escalates to the owner only when truly undecidable. Owner-specified items (e.g. request_sha256) are never removed as ceremony.

Owner rule (2026-11-07): follow .cursor/skills/cursor-orchestration exactly. Every QA round on every PR into integrate (docs PRs too) gets parent-spawned reviewers and then the cursor-quality-mgr enforcer, which renders and posts the report. The parent never renders or posts QA reports itself, and never merges without the enforcer's PR report. On FAIL, run /triaging-findings (.ttl) before fix dispatch. QA-2 reviewer set: req-qa, arch-qa, rust-qa (+flaky). A sprint flips its own status to complete in its own branch before merge; no separate closeout PRs.

Owner rule (2026-11-07): questions are answered in planning; dev<->QA runs end to end without stopping for the owner, with issues collected and addressed at the end. The TypeSafe Jev API (docs: .claude/skills/plan-anchoring/references/jev-api.md, POST /v1/systemone) is the source of truth; support ALL Jev question formats (choice/score/noul, keyed questions, state string|object|array) with schemas in sc-decision-schema. Answer spec questions by reading the spec/source (e.g. sc-sha crate source), never by asking the owner.
Owner rule (2026-11-07): the orchestrator syncs bd (bd dolt push) on every commit/push; never leave bead sync as an owner item.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): error contracts in every product follow the creating-ai-clis and reviewing-ai-clis skills: typed, discriminated results with a stable error id and message on every path. Reviews of CLI or library work must check against error-contracts.md and error-review.md; do not treat the generic Rust reviewers as covering this.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): the phase-ending review posts findings on the PR, and every review of fixes also posts its findings on the same PR, as soon as that review finishes, through the cursor-quality-mgr enforcer.
Owner rule (2026-11-08): everything in sc-agent is exposed to Python; the Python API may be more flexible than the CLI, never less.
Owner rule (2026-11-08): post the QA report as soon as QA is done; do not wait for CI. QA and CI are independent. Merging requires both CI and QA green.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): every sc-publish PR gets a careful QA agent review before merge. The agent rejects any change outside the requested scope and tests impact on all consumers of the kit by rendering and validating each one's real input against develop; 12 repos today: atm-core, sc-runtime, wyvern, sc-compose, beads-cache, docli, sc-agent, sc-lint, sc-observability, agent-team-mail, schook, atm-bd-orchestration. Why: a change that breaks a consumer causes weeks of churn, because each consumer then needs a PR every time it publishes; sc-compose, sc-observability and atm-core already do today and this must stop. Agents report the verdict; they do not post, approve, close or merge.
Owner rule (2026-11-08): on stacked PRs, fixes go on a new layer at the top, never mid-stack. This eliminates rebasing mid-stack.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): once a sprint's local tests pass and quality-mgr has cleared all findings, start the next sprint's dev immediately (branch from the cleared head if the merge is still pending); do not wait for CI or the merge.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): weekly token budget is tight. Use faster or cheaper models where possible: haiku for qa-triage, enforcer and doc-only reviewers; sonnet for code reviewers and developers. Keep prompts short, and avoid spawning redundant reviewers.

Owner rule (2026-11-08), verbatim: 'this is ONLY allowed in plan review. Any changes are approved by me.' REQ and ADR changes happen only during plan review and only with the owner's approval. Agents never change a REQ or ADR during development, fix rounds or QA, and never tell developers to. If a REQ or ADR doesn't support a change, stop and ask the owner. Carry this into the new repo.

Process rule (2026-11-08): after a usage-limit pause, check every subagent with ListAgents and compare it against its expected output (for example a PR comment or a pushed commit). Resume any agent that stopped before finishing, via SendMessage. A 'completed' status does not mean the work finished.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): idle time between dev finishing and QA starting makes the project take 2-4x longer. At every turn, check each branch's remote and local head against what was last reviewed, and start QA in that same message on anything new. Don't rely on an agent's report arriving, and never wait for CI, a rebase, or another layer.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): QA starts as soon as dev finishes a layer, before and independent of CI, and independent of lower layers landing. Never hold QA waiting for CI, a PR base, or a stack merge. Merging needs QA and CI both green.

Owner rule (2026-11-08): rebase or merge forward and stack layers as soon as they exist. QA or CI green isn't needed to stack; doing it earlier and more often lets more checks run in parallel. Merge forward is acceptable and safer than rebase. Fixes go on new top layers.
